items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had heard an orchestra by the name of Lois Dieppe once at Elmwood Town Hall

ctx.x: The first time I ever shot dice was with Edgar Hayes and Lee Rainey. One morning after we had arrived in the city, someone suggested that we have a crap game and I joined the party although I did not know much about the game. We played tit for tat until Lee finally became broke or tired and went to bed. We were all playing in his flat. Edgar and I kept playing head and head until I finally broke him. I had snapped my fingers so much that morning until I had rubbed the skin off my thumb and middle fingers, and the…

I had heard an orchestra by the name of Lois Dieppe once at Elmwood Town Hall which was another suburb of Cincinnati. In fact Dieppe was the first orchestra that I heard at Elmwood. Dieppe was from Columbus, Ohio, but I think his orchestra had played around Chicago and it was his first time to play in the vicinity of Cincinnati. There was no one in the orchestra that I gave special notice to except Lois who had such a powerful baritone voice that he stood behind the orchestra in back of the pianist and sang…
out their voices, and the orchestra did not have to soften their tone when Deppe sang.
